# DINOv2 inference benchmark (forward pass wall time, ms; lower is better).
#
# Generated by scripts/bench.sh. Order-of-magnitude seed values from the plan
# file at .agents/plans/2026-09-18-post-v0.2.0.md. Real numbers will be
# regenerated by the bench.yml manual-trigger workflow once PR C lands.
#
# Numbers here are placeholders, not measurements. Do not cite them as
# performance claims until the bench.yml workflow runs them.
#
# Methodology: 1 warmup + 5 timed runs, single 224x224 image (batch=1),
# --threads=min(4, hw_concurrency), f16 GGUF unless noted.
# Peak RSS is for the ViT-S column; it grows roughly linearly with model size
# (B ~3x, L ~10x, g ~40x). All rows exercise the CPU backend (Metal/CUDA
# are deferred -- see .agents/plans/2026-09-18-post-v0.2.0.md section 1).
# | Platform           | Arch   | ggml | ViT-S  | ViT-B  | ViT-L  | ViT-g   | Peak RSS (ViT-S) |
# |--------------------|--------|------|--------|--------|--------|---------|------------------|
# | macos-arm64 (M1)   | arm64  | cpu  |     72 |    198 |    580 |    1980 | 110 MB           |
# | ubuntu-x64 (Xeon)  | x86_64 | cpu  |    165 |    410 |   1190 |    4020 | 110 MB           |
# | ubuntu-arm64       | arm64  | cpu  |    140 |    360 |   1050 |    3550 | 110 MB           |
# | windows-x64        | x86_64 | cpu  |    170 |    420 |   1210 |    4080 | 110 MB           |
#
# Quantization sweep (ViT-S on ubuntu-x64 baseline):
# | Quant | mean (ms) | peak RSS |
# |-------|-----------|----------|
# | f16   |       165 |   109 MB |
# | q4_0  |        50 |    49 MB |
# | q4_1  |        50 |    52 MB |
# | q5_0  |        59 |    54 MB |
# | q5_1  |        57 |    57 MB |
# | q8_0  |        51 |    70 MB |
#
# Notes:
# - Numbers are seed values from order-of-magnitude estimates. Real numbers
#   will be regenerated by the bench.yml manual-trigger workflow (see
#   .agents/plans/2026-09-18-post-v0.2.0.md for the workflow design).
# - All rows exercise the CPU backend (Metal/CUDA CI is deferred).
# - Single 224x224 image (assets/tench.jpg or equivalent), batch=1,
#   1 warmup + 5 timed runs each cell, --threads=min(4, hw_concurrency).
